actions: Read .antfarm/queen.md, GOAL.md, AGENTS.md and DECISIONS.md, then inspected open Issues, open PRs and CI status via gh
Reviewed PR #41 (per-day notes, Issue #40) against all 11 acceptance criteria, including the full diff and the browser-evidence-35523887101 CI artifact screenshots at 360px and 1280px
Approved PR #41 with a written review recording which criteria were satisfied and that Codex raised no findings

Created Issue #42 'feat(nav): week paging and a jump-to-date control so past plans are reachable' with context, build instructions, 11 testable acceptance criteria, DECISIONS.md requirements and out-of-scope list, labelled ready
agent_report.summary:
Merged PR #41 (the per-day notes area, Issue #40) after verifying all 11 acceptance criteria against the diff and the CI browser-evidence screenshots: per-day notes storage normalised like existing optional keys, debounce+blur+beforeunload commit guarded by a noteDirty flag that fixes a genuine localStorage-clobbering bug, both i18n catalogues complete, sr-only label, 2000-char cap, no horizontal scroll at 360/1280px, and .notes-panel deliberately excluded from .panel so the #38 order test stays unmodified. Codex reviewed and raised no findings. That closes the last absent Daily Planning capability in GOAL.md.

With work in flight back to zero, created Issue #42 (labelled ready): week paging plus a native jump-to-date control in the header. Rationale recorded in the Issue — every GOAL.md capability now exists, so the most useful next work is the single friction that blocks a stated requirement ("past daily plans must remain accessible"): reaching a plan three weeks back currently costs ~21 clicks and last quarter is impractical. Criteria pin week paging, the date jump, followingToday behaviour from #14, cross-week work markers, both languages, keyboard access, no-scroll at four widths, and screenshot evidence.

Did not declare DONE: with #42 open the product has known friction against an explicit GOAL.md requirement, and DONE describes the state of the product, not the backlog. No blocked, human or request Issues were open this run.
